text: Atrophy (-ia) [Gr. atroqia , lack of nourishment]: Ger. Atrophie ; Fr. atrophie ; Ital. atrofia . Reduction in size or efficiency in an organ or mechanism of the body as a result of disuse, injury, or disease. Atrophy differs from degeneration in that the latter implies an actual destruction of the tissue. It is also distinguished from aplasy by careful writers. Cf. APLASY, and DEGENERATION. ( H.H .) In connection with the theory of evolution the term atrophy is now used for the diminution of an organ or tissue owing to its being useless (through change of habit or environment), or through its being superseded by some other organ. The inheritance of atrophy due to disuse is one of the tenets of the Lamarckian school of evolutionists. Literature : art. Atrophy, Encyc. Brit. (9th ed.); J. DEMOOR, J. MASSART, and E. VANDERVELDE, Evolution by Atrophy (1899). ( C.LL.M .)
